title: pathKnownToHistory confirms an exact literal path match, with quotePath/merge-commit rendering pinned
context: dec_aa1e430ea5 (now corrected/extended here) described a round-6 implementation that ran `git -c core.quotePath=false log -n1 --format= --name-only --diff-merges=first-parent HEAD -- :(literal)<file>` and checked the output for an exact NEWLINE-split line match. An eighth review round (mr-complexity-reviewer, PR #76 round 7 I1) found this closed only the non-ASCII slice of the quoting problem: git ALWAYS C-quotes a `"`, a backslash, or any control character regardless of core.quotePath, and the trimming `gitSafe` helper independently ate a real leading/trailing space in an unquoted name -- each reproduced as a false-positive refusal (a genuinely tracked, deleted-at-the-correct-root file misread as never-tracked) on a filename shaped like `q"uote.ts`, one containing a literal tab, or one with leading/trailing whitespace. A later review round (round 8) then found this record itself had gone uncaptured: round 7 rewrote the implementation but the live decision for this topic (dec_aa1e430ea5) still described the round-6 code, in the one repo whose stated product is detecting exactly that kind of doc/graph drift.
decision: pathKnownToHistory (src/extractors/git.ts) now runs `git log -n1 --format= --name-only -z --diff-merges=first-parent HEAD -- :(literal)<file>` via the UNTRIMMED gitRawSafe (not the trimming gitSafe), and checks the NUL-split output for an exact match. `-z` makes git emit the raw path bytes with NO escaping of any kind -- not just the >0x7F slice core.quotePath=false controls -- so core.quotePath is now irrelevant and dropped from the command entirely. Because `-z` NUL-TERMINATES (not separates) each entry, splitting on "\0" always yields a trailing empty-string element; pathKnownToHistory now explicitly rejects an empty `file` up front so that trailing artifact can never itself read as a match (round 8 M1) -- defense in depth for the function's own contract, since the sole caller already filters falsy entries first.
consequences: A filename containing a quote character, a control character (tab, literal newline), or genuine leading/trailing whitespace is now correctly recognized as known-to-history when deleted at the correct root -- closing the class round 6's narrower core.quotePath=false fix only partially closed

core.quotePath is no longer referenced by this function at all; this is a deliberate, narrow exception to dec_cb855e5d0f ("pin core.quotePath=false per git command") because -z makes the setting moot for this specific command rather than because the convention was rejected
pathKnownToHistory(root, "") now explicitly returns false rather than depending on the sole caller's own falsy-filter to avoid ever reaching it
alternatives_rejected: Add core.quotePath=false AND handle quote/control-character escaping separately -- rejected: this is exactly the one-byte-class-at-a-time patching that produced rounds 4 through 6's repeated re-openings of this same class; -z removes the entire escaping mechanism at once instead of enumerating more byte ranges to except from it

Leave core.quotePath=false in the command for consistency with dec_cb855e5d0f even though -z makes it inert -- rejected as dead configuration that would misleadingly suggest quoting is still a live concern for a reader who doesn't already know -z supersedes it; the doc comment records the exception explicitly instead
